text.title: WebSocket Design Failure Modes
text.summary: 8 antipatterns observed in real deployments. Each pairs symptom + root cause + concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: The client crashes as soon as the server adds a field to a payload; every additive protocol change becomes a coordinated release.
antipattern.root-cause: Messages are raw JSON with no envelope and no version, so there is nothing to negotiate against and no rule that unknown fields are ignorable.
antipattern.fix: Adopt the {v, type, channel, id, seq, ts, payload} envelope; clients ignore unknown fields within the same v, and v is bumped only for genuinely breaking changes. See rule versioned-envelope.

antipattern.symptom: The connection looks alive on the client while the server dropped it four minutes ago; messages vanish with no error.
antipattern.root-cause: No application-level heartbeat — the design relied on TCP keep-alive, whose defaults fire far too late.
antipattern.fix: Ping every 25–30 s, close after 2 missed pongs, let the client reconnect on the close. See rule heartbeat-required.

antipattern.symptom: Server OOMs after one client stopped reading; metrics show 50M messages queued on a single connection.
antipattern.root-cause: The per-connection outgoing queue was unbounded, so one slow reader consumed the whole process heap.
antipattern.fix: Bound the queue, declare shed_policy=drop_oldest, and close with code 1008 once shedding crosses a threshold. See rule bounded-send-queue.

antipattern.symptom: A malformed payload from one client raises inside the handler and takes down the whole connection loop.
antipattern.root-cause: Message types had no JSON schema, so handlers indexed fields that the sender never had to provide.
antipattern.fix: Attach a JSON schema to every message type and validate on both ends; reject with close code 1008 or an error envelope rather than raising. See rule schema-validated-per-type.

antipattern.symptom: The client cannot tell a deploy from a ban: every disconnect arrives as a bare close, so it reconnects into a rejection loop.
antipattern.root-cause: Server closed the socket without an RFC 6455 code, or sent 1000 for every case including policy violations.
antipattern.fix: Emit a truthful code — 1001 on shutdown, 1008 on policy violation, 1009 on oversize, 4xxx for app reasons — and branch the client's reconnect on it. See rule close-code-truthful.

antipattern.symptom: WebSocket URL contains ?token=eyJ... appearing in access logs.
antipattern.root-cause: Browsers cannot send custom headers on WebSocket upgrade; author chose the easy path.
antipattern.fix: Use a one-shot ticket from POST /ws-ticket exchanged for a session cookie or short-lived URL param that is logged-scrubbed.

antipattern.symptom: One misbehaving client floods the event loop and starves all other clients on the process.
antipattern.root-cause: Author treated WebSocket like UDP — no per-connection ceiling.
antipattern.fix: Apply per-connection token bucket (e.g. 30 msgs/sec) and per-user connection cap (3–5).

antipattern.symptom: Deploy completes; every client reconnects at the same second and the auth endpoint falls over.
antipattern.root-cause: Linear or fixed-delay reconnect with no randomisation.
antipattern.fix: Replace with full-jitter exponential backoff capped at 30s.

antipattern.symptom: ConnectionManager state stored at module scope; horizontal scaling silently breaks fan-out.
antipattern.fix: Keep ConnectionManager per-process; push fan-out to Redis Pub/Sub.
